> 剝。不利有攸往。

Hexagram 23 is about something wearing away, and its character is the book's one instance of the opposite error.

## 剝 is 從刀從錄，錄亦聲

說文: 剝，裂也。從刀，從錄。錄，刻割也。錄亦聲.

Original sense: to split, to flay open. The structure is 刀 plus 錄 — and 錄 is simultaneously the sound.

So this is a 會意 with 亦聲, a picture that also carries its own pronunciation.

And the gloss the book has to correct is the reverse of its usual correction. Four chapters ago the error was turning phonetics into pictures (訟, 謙, 觀, 賁). Here 剝's 錄 is a sound that got dropped, and the word was flattened into a single image: a knife scraping.

The root is the same in both directions: if the way the character is built is not settled, interpretation comes in and takes the place of the character's sense.

So 剝 is not primarily "a knife peeling something." It is a split. The gradual erosion — 以刀慢慢削蝕 — is an extension.

## 剝床以足

The bed is the thing you rest on: the base of the body, the seat of what carries you.

And the erosion starts at the feet — 剝床以足 — and moves upward:

- 足: the legs of the bed. The foundation.
- 辨: the joint between leg and frame, the trunk of the bed. Now the main body is being eaten.
- 膚: the surface of the bed, the part next to the person lying on it.

Three lines, one direction: from the ground up, until the damage is against the body.

Which is the hexagram's mechanism, and it is a schedule rather than a warning. Decay does not arrive at the top. It climbs.

## 蔑貞

蔑 has two glosses: 滅, to extinguish (釋文: 蔑，猶滅也), and 輕, to treat lightly (Zheng Xuan: 蔑，輕也).

This book keeps both together: the standard is held lightly, and so it fades. Contempt and disappearance are the same process seen at two moments.

## 貫魚，以宮人寵

六五 貫魚，以宮人寵，無不利.

Fish strung together in order, one behind another: sequence, no one pushing ahead.

宮人: those who serve within, keeping to their own place, not reaching outward for power.

This is the one line in the hexagram with 無不利, and it is the line where nothing is being taken. The image of the correct response to erosion is not resistance. It is order: everyone in sequence, no one leaping the queue.

## 碩果不食

Top line: 碩果不食，君子得輿，小人剝廬.

A great fruit not eaten. Every other fruit has been stripped; this one remains — the last seed, the surviving yang.

And then the split verdict: the noble gets a carriage (輿, what carries people), the small man strips the hut (廬, what one lives in).

Same situation, same object, two outcomes. Which is the most economical statement of the difference in the whole book: presented with the last seed, one person treats it as something to ride, the other as something to eat.

## 厚下安宅

The 象: thicken what is below, make the dwelling secure.

厚下 — feed the base. Not reinforce the top, not patch the surface. The hexagram has just shown that the erosion begins at the feet, and its instruction is accordingly at the bottom: whatever is holding the structure up needs to be made thicker.

Which is a strikingly unglamorous answer to decline, and it is the only one the chapter gives.

## The test

Take an institution or a body you care about that is declining. Locate the line: is the erosion in the legs (the base that carries everything), in the joint (the connection between base and body), or in the surface (the part touching the person)? Most diagnoses name the surface, because that is where it is felt. The hexagram says that by then it has been climbing for a while.
